name: mug

name: kite

name: owl

name: books

name: car

name: lightbulb

name: checklist

name: headphones

name: magnifier

name: page-pencil
about: A page with a pencil. Writing, notes, drafting, creating something new.

name: gear
about: Gears. Systems, processes, how things work, machinery.

name: robot
about: A friendly robot. AI, agents, automation.

name: robot-scan
about: A robot scanning a page. AI reading, research, finding information.

name: robot-report
about: A robot sharing a checked result. AI reporting back, completing a task.

name: sprout
about: A sprout. Growth, learning, starting small, progress.

name: puzzle
about: Two puzzle pieces fitting together. Collaboration, integration, parts of a solution.

name: laptop
about: A laptop. Computers, coding, working online.

name: chat
about: Two speech bubbles. Conversation, feedback, asking questions.

name: compass
about: A compass. Direction, strategy, finding your way, goals.

name: sticky-note
about: A sticky note. Ideas on a wall, workshops, capturing a thought.

name: learner
about: A person reading a book with headphones on. Studying, learning, taking something in.

name: explainer
about: A person pointing up with an idea. Explaining, teaching, a tip or insight.

name: waver
about: A person waving. Hello, welcome, getting someone's attention, goodbye.

name: coffee
about: A person holding a mug of coffee. Relaxed, a break, informal chat.

name: pointer
about: A person pointing up with an idea. An alternative to the explainer.

name: cat
about: A sitting cat, winking. Playful aside, a light moment.

name: dog
about: A sitting dog with its head tilted. Curiosity, a question, loyalty.

name: group
about: Four people and a dog side by side. A team, a community, working together.

name: Title on highlighter
about: Big marker caps on a yellow highlighter swash. Wrap each line's words in .sk-hl; add .sk-burst for the tick marks.

name: Section heading
about: Label caps in deep teal with a rule either side.

name: Step panel
about: A numbered step in one of the five main colours. Add .sk-dashed for a dotted outline, to highlight the step you're talking about. Use .sk-em for accent text.

name: Speech bubble
about: Something a person says or asks. Add .sk-tail-right to move the tail to the right.
html: “I want to learn Chapter 1 of Shape Up, while I’m driving.”

name: Ribbon banner
about: An insight or takeaway. The kicker word goes in .sk-kicker, and an icon is optional.
html: Insight: “I want to learn a book while driving.”

name: Arrows
about: A short slate connector between steps, and the blue loop-back arrow that sits under a row of panels. Their colours come from the CSS.
html:

name: Panel wash
about: Add .sk-wash to a panel for a pale wash of its accent colour mixed with the page, about 9%. Use it to set a card apart from the page.

name: Highlighter anywhere
about: .sk-hl works outside a title too: on a phrase, or on a whole row to mark the one you're on. Add .sk-sweep to sweep it in once, for a moment worth marking; it stays still for people who ask for less motion.

name: Tick
about: A hand-drawn tick for something done or passing. It takes the size of the text around it, and the forest text colour; set color to change it. Give it a label when it stands alone.
html: Three Examples hold.

name: Buttons
about: .sk-btn is the one main action on a screen: deep teal with paper lettering. Add .sk-secondary for the others: an ink outline.
html:
<button class="sk-btn" type="button">Start the course →</button>
<button class="sk-btn sk-secondary" type="button">Use a different project</button>

name: Progress meter
about: A wobbly bar. Set --sk-value from 0% to 100%; the fill takes the accent, so a colour modifier changes it. Put the count in words next to it.
html: 3 of 10 Examples hold

name: Whole slide
about: A complete 16:9 slide built only from kit pieces. Start from this.
